report.biggest_gap_example: "Supported deployment pipelines, occasionally managing staging environments." does not show what you changed or the result, so the depth of your release ownership is unclear.
report.first_impression: The NovaTech role has useful numbers around retention, uptime, response time, and manual data entry. Earlier work is more duty-focused, and the caregiving break needs a cleaner return-to-work frame.
gaps: Your current target is not defined beyond a broad software engineering label, so recruiters must infer whether backend, platform, or full-stack work is the priority.
Several BrightWave and ClearPath bullets describe participation or support without naming the system size, decision, or result.
The return after caregiving is acknowledged, but the summary does not name the recent coursework or personal projects that demonstrate current readiness.

questions.why: The 99.9% uptime result becomes more useful when its operating scale is clear.

questions.why: A specific incident would show judgment beyond routine support participation.

questions.question: What changed in your testing or review process alongside the 15% increase in test coverage?
questions.why: The coverage number is useful, but the engineering action behind it is not yet visible.

questions.why: The dashboard result is strong; the full delivery path would establish the boundaries of your ownership.

report.score_comment_long: The resume contains multiple specific outcomes and credible ownership signals. Evidence is not equally strong in every role. Tightening the weakest bullets will make the story easier to place.
report.score_comment_short: Several concrete outcomes are visible, with a few uneven areas still limiting the first read.
report.score_plain: This has a credible evidence base. Strengthen the few thin bullets instead of rewriting what already works.

Education.fix: Add only if it supports the target role or removes a stated requirement question.

Work Experience.fix: Add scale and outcomes to BrightWave and ClearPath bullets, while preserving support and assisted ownership where those are accurate.
Work Experience.missing: Several bullets omit application scale, incident detail, deployment responsibility, and results.
Work Experience.working: NovaTech shows measurable reliability, performance, retention, and workflow results, plus mentoring and migration work.

strengths: The NovaTech microservices bullet combines direct ownership with 99.9% uptime and approximately 20% faster API response times, making the backend contribution easy to place.
The dashboard work links development and deployment to a 10% increase in client retention, which gives one project a clear business reason to keep.
Java, Spring Boot, AWS, Docker, Jenkins, SQL, and RESTful APIs form a coherent technical base for backend applications.
report.summary: NovaTech gives you a credible mid-level backend foundation: microservices, APIs, AWS migration, and measurable reliability and workflow gains. The 99.9% uptime and 20% faster response times are worth keeping because they show production responsibility, not just feature work. Your earlier roles add Java, Spring Boot, testing, and client support, but many bullets stop at participation. The practical question is what you built or maintained during the 2022-2024 break, since that will shape how recruiters judge your current technical readiness.
